title: React Components & Props
summary: Breaks a React app into small, reusable components. Parents pass data down to children with props (one-way data flow), props can be destructured for cleaner code, and state can live in a child (just that card) or be lifted to a parent when several children need it. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Split UI into components, pass data with props, and decide whether state belongs in the parent or the child.

steps.title: Read both lessons
steps.detail: Read 'Components and Props' and 'Component Level State', especially 'When should a state live at parent vs child'.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain the difference between props and state.

steps.title: Trace a prop in Myflix
steps.detail: Myflix already does this. In assignments/week-02/netflix/src/views/MyList.jsx the parent renders <ShowCard key={entry.show.id} entry={entry} onOpen={setOpenId} />, and ShowCard.jsx destructures ({ entry, onOpen }). onOpen is a function prop: the child calls it, the parent's state changes.
steps.doneWhen: You can say which component owns openId and how the card changes it.

steps.title: Classify Myflix state
steps.detail: Pick three pieces of state in Myflix (for example openId, a star rating, a comment draft) and decide for each: child-level or parent-level? Use the lesson's rule of thumb: if several components need it, lift it up.
steps.doneWhen: You have a three-line list with a reason for each choice.

concepts.meaning: A function that returns a piece of UI and can be reused.
Inputs a parent passes to a child component, read-only inside the child.
Writing ({ entry, onOpen }) to pull props out by name.
Data moves down from parent to child; children report up by calling functions.
Moving state to the nearest shared parent so several children can use it.
